To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the expression profiles of radiation-induced rat osteosarcoma were compared with those in normal osteoblast, (2) 72 genes were found differentially expressed between the tumors and normal cells, (3) the expression profiles suggested that the Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway is activated in the tumors, and (4) the activation of Wnt/beta catenin signaling was confirmed in the tumors by using immunohistochemistry and Western blotting.

we identified several genes involved in radiation-induced OS, including genes involved in the Src tyrosine kinases and Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathways, and confirmed the activation of beta-catenin and the reduction in the level of GSK-3beta in the tumors, which may be important for radiation-induced OS.

we have identified a group of genes that may be involved in radiation‐ induced osteosarcoma and that these genes are associated with cell adhesion, differentiation, developmental processes, tumor‐ suppressor function, Src tyrosine signaling, and Wnt/ β‐catenin signaling pathways.

radiation‐induced bone tumors have a unique gene expression profile that is different from that of normal osteoblastic cells, and that this profile includes several genes involved in the negative regulation of the Wnt/beta‐catenin signaling.
